summary.headline: Dr Reddy's Q1 FY27 revenue fell 5.6% YoY to ₹8,071 crore on lenalidomide base effect and a ₹240 crore semaglutide API provision; underlying EBITDA margin 12.5%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was ₹8,071 crore (US$853 million), down 5.6% YoY but up 7.4% QoQ, as lower lenalidomide sales offset strong base-business growth and favourable forex. Reported gross margin fell to 46.5% (49.4% excluding the semaglutide API provision) and EBITDA margin to 12.5% (15.4% excluding the provision). Management attributed the hit to semaglutide supply disruption, lost PLI incentives, and Middle East-driven solvent and freight costs (about 1% of EBITDA). Management said semaglutide commercial supply is planned to resume by November, and it reiterated that the company expects a strong second half.

segments.name: North America Generics
segments.commentary: Revenue US$236 million (27% of total), down 41% YoY on lenalidomide base effect but up 19% QoQ; base business grew double digits with six launches including bosutinib and nintedanib.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,833 crore (23% of total), up 31% YoY and 2% QoQ; 43 new product launches in the quarter.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,718 crore (21% of total), up 17% YoY and 10% QoQ; organic growth ex acquisitions 15.5%; IQVIA MAT growth 13.5% vs market 11.1%; IPM rank 9th for quarter.

segments.name: Europe (incl. NRT)
segments.commentary: Revenue €131 million (18% of total), broadly flat YoY and down 3% QoQ on price erosion and NRT operating-model change; 24 new generic launches.

segments.name: PSAI
segments.commentary: Revenue US$91 million (11% of total), down 5% YoY and 10% QoQ on lower API volume uptake; 38 Drug Master Files filed.

guidance_outlook: Semaglutide commercial supply expected to resume by November; API testing to finish around the third week of September, with 6-7 million pens targeted for November to March.

Management maintains EBITDA margin in the neighbourhood of 20% excluding semaglutide, and expects the next quarter (without semaglutide) to be around 20%; margins to be higher once semaglutide returns.
Full-year tax rate guided at 24-25%; R&D at 7-8% of revenue (closer to 7% this year).
FY27 capex guided at around ₹1,800 crore, with similar levels expected next year.
SG&A to stay broadly in line with FY26 absolute level; sales growth in double digits versus low-single-digit cost growth.
US base business (ex lenalidomide and semaglutide) guided for double-digit growth through the year; 27 US launches targeted for FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Gross margin ex semaglutide API provision

financial_highlights.change: vs 26% in Q1 FY26; benefited from reversal of tax provisions

qa_highlights.question: How will margins improve from the high-teens ex-semaglutide level toward the 20% guidance, given uncertainty over semaglutide timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excluding semaglutide and Middle East impacts, Q1 margin was about 18%, versus 19% last quarter; it reiterated a neighbourhood of 20% including next quarter (still without semaglutide), with margins higher once semaglutide returns in November.

qa_highlights.question: Why did US revenue fall QoQ despite bosutinib and Canada launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing unusual happened; it reflected procurement timing, the bosutinib launch was successful, and US double-digit growth is maintained for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of abatacept after the seven Form 483 observations, and is there any query on the BLA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the observations differ from the prior inspection's five, are addressable, and responses were sent to USFDA on Friday; no BLA query received so far and the December goal date remains; abatacept was filed only from Bachupally.

qa_highlights.question: How much semaglutide pen volume was lost to the API provision, and what is the confidence in 6-7 million pens?
qa_highlights.answer: About 180,000 pens sold before stoppage; opportunity lost about 3-4 million pens assuming a November return; management said confidence is high given backed orders and approvals expected in several markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the guidance for tax rate, R&D and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year tax rate 24-25%; R&D 7-8% of revenue, closer to 7% this year; FY27 capex around ₹1,800 crore, with similar levels next year.

qa_highlights.question: Did management quantify the root-cause and resolution probability for semaglutide API?
qa_highlights.answer: Root cause identified; program management points to around September 22-23; management put the success probability at 80-90%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the risks to the US generics business and what are the tariff implications?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the US generic market is at best single-digit growth absent upsides; on tariffs it said the announcement is not yet actionable and it is not giving it much weight, with about 25-30% of revenue already made by US CMOs.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at around ₹1,800 crore, with management expecting similar levels next year; capex had been ₹2,500-2,700 crore in earlier years, cut to ₹1,800 crore, with continued product-specific spend in biosimilars and peptides
Q1 FY27 capex cash outflow ₹307 crore (US$32 million)

Semaglutide API: theoretical capacity up to 550 (needs scale-up), and north of 300 without expansion; API made at Vizag CTO-6 USFDA-approved plant; API testing to finish around third week of September, then supply to partner OneSource

Abatacept is made at own Bachupally facility (CCM5 drug substance, FFM2 fill-finish); USFDA pre-licence inspection in June 2026 ended with Form 483 of seven observations, responded to; BLA goal date mid-December 2026, no queries received as of call date
Abatacept subcutaneous launch expected around Feb/March 2028 in US and around September-October 2028 in Europe; biologics ~2% of sales, expected profitable from abatacept launch
Peptides and biologics facilities have capacity created; management did not quantify current cost drag from these facilities (to come back on it)
demand_pricing: Underlying base business excluding lenalidomide grew double digits across key geographies including North America; US base business (ex lenalidomide and semaglutide) guided for double-digit growth through FY27

North America Generics US$236 million, down 41% YoY on lenalidomide base effect, up 19% QoQ; management attributed QoQ dip to procurement timing, not destocking; bosutinib launched with two weeks of supply in the quarter
India revenue ₹1,718 crore, up 17% YoY and 10% QoQ; organic growth 15.5%; IQVIA MAT growth 13.5% vs IPM 11.1%; IPM rank 9th for quarter
Emerging Markets growth north of 15% and in some places above 20%, per management

Semaglutide: 180,000 pens sold before supply stopped; 6-7 million pens targeted for November to March, with management citing backed orders; lost about 4 months of sales (from 10-11 million to 6-7 million pens); opportunity lost about 3-4 million pens

Canada semaglutide price CAD 78 before channel margins; retail/private channel margin 38% and additional 5-6% to provinces where reimbursed; no further price cut expected as three players are in market; Sandoz commitment still holds
Europe revenue €131 million, flat YoY, down 3% QoQ on price erosion and NRT operating-model change; NRT rebates now netted in revenue, profit neutral
PSAI US$91 million, down 5% YoY and 10% QoQ on lower API volume uptake
Gross margin ex provision 49.4% (Global Generics 53.8%, PSAI 12.9%); Middle East solvent and freight costs about 1% of EBITDA, expected to persist at least through December
SG&A ₹2,882 crore (36% of revenue); management said ~75-80% of the increase YoY and QoQ was due to forex and Middle East freight; target sales growth in double digits vs low-single-digit cost growth

Bosutinib 400 mg market about US$300 million; margin above company average; semaglutide Canada: management said ex-provision EBITDA margin in high-teens (about 18%), with next quarter ex-semaglutide around 20%
risks_watch: Semaglutide API scale-up: resumption targeted for November, depends on API testing finishing around third week of September and a 80-90% success probability per management; any slip cuts the 6-7 million pen target further
Competitive entry in Canada semaglutide (third player approved, a fourth targeted for December end) could pressure pricing and rebates when supply resumes
Abatacept BLA goal date mid-December 2026; any additional GMP or BLA queries could delay launch, which is key for FY28 and biologics breakeven
Middle East conflict: solvent and freight costs about 1% of EBITDA, expected to persist at least until December
Lost PLI incentives: no PLI in Q1 FY27; accrual resumes only after semaglutide growth thresholds are met; US tariff announcement on generics is unresolved
key_quotes: So, nothing happened, it's actually in the right direction.
We remain confident of a strong second half of the fiscal, with the resumption of semaglutide supplies.
No, we have plenty of capacity.
So, we are not changing the specs or the quality. It was just our ability to meet the specs in the scale-up batch of the API, which we need to resolve.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the second-half recovery and the 20% margin neighbourhood, but cautious and at times defensive on semaglutide timing and US growth, repeatedly stressing that the API issue is a quality, not capacity, problem. Management was evasive on the cost drag from the peptide and biologics facilities and on the quantified PLI accrual.

adds.what: Semaglutide API capacity at Vizag CTO-6 USFDA-approved plant (theoretical up to 550, north of 300 without expansion; needs scale-up)
Abatacept subcutaneous biologic launch (own Bachupally CCM5/FFM2 facilities; BLA goal mid-Dec 2026, launch ~Feb/Mar 2028 US)

growth.why: Management reiterates double-digit base business growth and a strong H2 FY27 with semaglutide supply resuming by November (6-7 million pens Nov-Mar, backed by orders per management), plus 27 US launches targeted; backing is partly specific (pen volumes, launch count, Vizag API capacity) but no revenue guidance number is given.
